newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil dips on IPE, barges sold aggressively.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil dips on IPE, barges sold aggressively.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices slipped on IPE futures on Thursday but premiums for low sulphur diesel remained firm amid tight supplies and heating oil premiums were holding despite evidence of growing supply, traders said.
Nov IPE fell $1.50 to $226.00 per tonne on further profit-taking ahead of a U.S. Energy Department meeting with the oil industry on Friday to address low inventories.
On the cargo market, heating oil was offered unchanged at Nov +$7 cif NWE for late Oct, with buying interest at +$6.
A German winter grade low sulphur diesel cargo was discussed at Nov IPE +$34/36.
A French GOM diesel cargo was offered at Nov IPE +$32 for late October delivery and +$30 for early Nov, also unchanged from Wednesday, traders said.
Traders said one result of Friday's U.S. talks could be a ban on exports.

Large quantities of U.S. origin heating oil were being sold aggressively into the Rotterdam barge market at around Nov IPE +$2 fob ARA, bringing the value of refinery grade barges down to +$3.50, traders said. In Flushing, barges traded at Nov IPE +$5.00 and +$3.50 fob.
